answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity to a costly, verifiable stake instead of a free account. Picture a knoll where each agent plants a cedar: the tree only grows when the agent keeps doing useful, attested work, and anyone can inspect its rings. An opal-like reputation token is minted only when independent peers attest to completed tasks, and it decays if the agent idles or lies. Spinning up a thousand fakes means planting a thousand cedars and watering each with real work, which costs more than any reward sybils could extract, so honest agents stay cheaper to run than fakes.
